Outcome: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organization related to the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks are in place, transparent, and implemented effectively
Observation: No AI policy or acceptable use policy. AI is not mentioned in the Information Security Policy. AI-specific legal and regulatory requirements are not tracked.
Recommendation: Approve the AI Acceptable Use Policy and an AI Governance Policy; add AI laws (EU AI Act, state AI laws, Section 1557) to the obligations register.

Outcome: Accountability structures are in place so that the appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible, and trained for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks
Observation: No named AI risk owner. The data science lead informally owns ReadmitIQ. No AI training for any role.
Recommendation: Form an AI Governance Committee (CISO, VP Product, Legal, Privacy, Data Science, Clinical Advisor); assign an owner to every AI system; launch AI literacy training.

Outcome: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility processes are prioritized in the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks throughout the lifecycle
Observation: ReadmitIQ design decisions were made by a three-person data science team with no clinical, legal, or patient-perspective input.
Recommendation: Require review by a clinical advisor and Legal/Privacy for AI systems that affect patients; include patient-advocate input for high-risk systems.

Outcome: Organizational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk
Observation: Engineering runs blameless postmortems and design reviews, but AI risks are not a standard design-review topic.
Recommendation: Add AI risk questions to the design review template; share AI incidents and near misses in engineering all-hands.

Outcome: Processes are in place for robust engagement with relevant AI actors
Observation: No channel for customers, care managers, or patients to report problems with AI outputs.
Recommendation: Add in-product feedback on AI outputs (thumbs down and report); route to the AI system owner with a triage SLA.

Outcome: Policies and procedures are in place to address AI risks and benefits arising from third-party software and data and other supply chain issues
Observation: The LLM provider, SaaS AI features, and the ATS were never assessed for AI risk. Contracts have no AI-specific clauses (e.g., no training on customer data).
Recommendation: Add an AI module to vendor due diligence; require no-training and data-retention clauses; inventory AI features in existing SaaS tools.

Observation: ReadmitIQ's intended use is described in a 2024 product spec. Other AI systems have no documented intended use, users, or deployment context.
Recommendation: Document intended purpose, users, affected persons, and deployment context for every inventoried AI system.

Outcome: Categorization of the AI system is performed
Observation: No risk tiering of AI systems and no regulatory classification (EU AI Act, EU MDR, FDA) before this assessment.
Recommendation: Adopt the risk tiering in this assessment; obtain a regulatory determination for ReadmitIQ; classify every new AI use case at intake.

Outcome: AI capabilities, targeted usage, goals, and expected benefits and costs compared with appropriate benchmarks are understood
Observation: Benefits are documented for ReadmitIQ and Support Copilot, but neither is benchmarked against a non-AI baseline, and known limitations are not documented.
Recommendation: Document limitations and out-of-scope uses; benchmark ReadmitIQ against the standard LACE index used by hospitals.

Outcome: Risks and benefits are mapped for all components of the AI system including third-party software and data
Observation: Risks of third-party models and training data are not mapped. The legal basis for using PHI from 12 customers to train ReadmitIQ is undocumented.
Recommendation: Create data lineage records for training data; complete Legal review of BAA permitted uses; map component risks in the AI risk register.

Outcome: Impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society are characterized
Observation: No assessment of how ReadmitIQ errors affect patients or specific demographic groups.
Recommendation: Perform an AI impact assessment for ReadmitIQ, ATS candidate ranking, and Support Copilot.

Outcome: Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied
Observation: ReadmitIQ accuracy (AUROC) was measured at launch. No metrics exist for the generative AI systems.
Recommendation: Define metrics per system: AUROC, calibration and subgroup performance for ReadmitIQ; groundedness, refusal, and escalation rates for Support Copilot.

Outcome: AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics
Observation: One fairness check in 2024. No robustness, privacy, or security testing; Support Copilot was never red-teamed.
Recommendation: Run bias testing across race, ethnicity, sex, age, and payer; red-team Support Copilot against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications before each major release.

Outcome: Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place
Observation: No production monitoring for model drift, performance decay, or emerging risks.
Recommendation: Deploy model monitoring with alert thresholds for drift, calibration, and subgroup performance; review monthly.

Outcome: Feedback about efficacy of measurement is gathered and assessed
Observation: No process to check whether chosen metrics reflect real-world outcomes.
Recommendation: Compare predicted risk with actual readmissions quarterly with two pilot customers; review metric relevance annually.

Outcome: AI risks based on assessments and other analytical output from the MAP and MEASURE functions are prioritized, responded to, and managed
Observation: AI risks were not in any risk register before this assessment.
Recommendation: Maintain the AI risk register as part of the enterprise risk register; review quarterly at the AI Governance Committee.

Outcome: Strategies to maximize AI benefits and minimize negative impacts are planned, prepared, implemented, documented, and informed by input from relevant AI actors
Observation: Support Copilot can be switched off with a feature flag, but there are no documented go/no-go criteria or rollback procedures for AI releases.
Recommendation: Define release gates (evaluation thresholds, sign-offs) and documented rollback procedures for every AI system.

Outcome: AI risks and benefits from third-party entities are managed
Observation: The LLM provider's model upgrades are applied automatically; SaaS AI features are enabled by vendors without review.
Recommendation: Pin model versions; run regression evaluations before upgrades; review SaaS AI feature settings quarterly.

Outcome: Risk treatments, including response and recovery, and communication plans for the identified and measured AI risks are documented and monitored regularly
Observation: The incident response plan has no AI scenarios (harmful output, bias complaint, jailbreak, model failure).
Recommendation: Add AI incident playbooks to the IR plan; define criteria for notifying customers of AI incidents.
